---
title: "Homework 1 Recap"
---

## Overall

- A strong first effort. The class mean was 27.8 out of 30.
- Grades and comments are posted in Canvas, so read your comment.
- A few things came up across several submissions, and they are all worth carrying into Homework 2.

## Getting the data right

- Pull each premium from the correct source column and plan-year.
- The most common lost points were premiums that did not match the filed rates.
- Check your numbers against the source before you interpret them.

## Building the national rate

- Build the national Medicare rate from the two county files: merge on FIPS and year, then count-weight (sum the counts, then divide).
- Averaging the county rates, or reading in a ready-made national file, does not earn full credit.
- Do the build in the notebook itself, so anyone can reproduce it.

## Committing your work

- Commit the dataset your code actually produces, not a file left in a gitignored `data/` folder.
- Use git: commit and push from a local clone, rather than uploading files through the website.
- Keep your repository private.

## Making the argument

- Q1(d) asked for a verdict. Name the alternatives and weigh them against your data before you land on one.
- Listing "other factors" without weighing them is not a verdict.
- State the mechanism, do not just name it.

## Working with AI

- The tool writes code and prose quickly. Your job is to check it.
- Read everything before you submit it.
- If AI hands you a citation, confirm the source is real and that it supports your point.
